condition: suspected febrile infected urolithiasis presenting with right lumbar flank aching urinary gravel passage and 39 C fever
level_rationale: A 39 C fever today in an adult with 2 days of right lumbar-flank aching after passing gritty urinary gravel yesterday indicates suspected infected urolithiasis or obstructive pyelonephritis with urosepsis risk requiring immediate emergency hospital intravenous antibiotics, cultures, and urgent imaging, whereas an afebrile 37 C temperature today with a 2-day lower-back and right-side ache after passing gritty sand yesterday warrants routine outpatient physician stone follow-up and urinalysis.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice single measured-temperature control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (2-day lower-back and right-flank ache, passing gritty urinary gravel yesterday, and measured 39 C temperature today) with a 2-word span difference (16 vs 18 words) and 12 shared trailing tokens ('a 39 C temperature today so I need to go to the'). Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing only the measured temperature in f3 from '39 C' to '37 C' keeps the exact same urinary-gravel case while shifting care cleanly from emergency hospital sepsis management (level 4) to routine outpatient physician stone follow-up (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
